Welcome to Thames View Primary School
Thames View, which is part of the well-respected Howard Academy Trust (THAT), has some real strengths, namely the wonderful cohort of children, an excellent staff team and fantastic school grounds, all of which we intend to make the most of during the coming year.
Belonging here. Shaping the world.
We are a two-form entry school, and with our Nursery, educate 480 children in a friendly and caring environment.
Our Curriculum
At Thames View, every child is known, valued and supported to thrive. Our curriculum helps pupils understand themselves, their community and the wider world, so they develop as confident, curious and responsible Global Citizens.
Ethos & Values
We promote our values of respect, responsibility and resilience, throughout all we do, so that our pupils are ready to take their place in a constantly changing world.

PSHCE
At Thames View, PSHCE helps pupils develop the knowledge, confidence and vocabulary they need to understand themselves, build positive relationships, stay safe and make responsible choices. Pupils learn about feelings, friendships, difference, safety, health, wellbeing, rights, responsibilities and growing up.
Our PSHCE curriculum is taught through the Coram SCARF scheme of learning and is shaped around the needs, context and experiences of pupils at Thames View.
Our Learning
How PSHCE develops Global Citizens
PSHCE helps pupils become respectful, responsible and resilient Global Citizens. Through PSHCE, pupils learn how to value themselves and others, respect difference, build healthy relationships, look after their wellbeing and contribute positively to their school, community and wider world.
Pupils are encouraged to think carefully about their choices, understand the impact they can have on others, and develop the confidence to ask for help when they need it.
Our PSHCE Narrative Threads
Our PSHCE curriculum is organised around four narrative threads. These help pupils revisit important personal, social, health and relationship themes over time, moving from early understanding of self and friendship to more complex learning about responsibility, safety, wellbeing, puberty and healthy relationships.
Pupils learn to understand themselves, recognise feelings, build positive friendships and develop a sense of belonging. They explore kindness, cooperation, self-respect, family, friendship, difference and how to seek help when relationships feel difficult or unsafe.
Pupils learn to value difference, challenge unfairness and understand their rights and responsibilities. They explore diversity, stereotypes, prejudice, bullying, democracy, money, the environment and how their choices can help make their school and community fairer and kinder.
Pupils learn how to keep themselves and others safe, healthy and well. They explore risk, decision-making, online safety, medicines, legal drugs, sleep, hygiene, exercise, healthy eating, mental wellbeing, media influence and how to ask trusted adults for help.
Pupils learn about families, friendships, privacy, safe and unsafe touch, personal boundaries, body changes, puberty, menstrual wellbeing and how to get help. This thread supports pupils to understand themselves and others, use correct vocabulary, recognise when something feels unsafe and develop the confidence to speak to a trusted adult.
How we teach PSHCE
In PSHCE, pupils revisit prior learning before being introduced to new knowledge, vocabulary and ideas. They learn through discussion, stories, scenarios, role play, reflection, questioning, carefully chosen resources and age-appropriate activities.
Pupils are taught to think carefully and respectfully by listening to others, sharing ideas, asking questions, considering different viewpoints and reflecting on choices. Teachers create safe and supportive opportunities for pupils to talk about important issues, while making clear where pupils can go for help.
From Year 1 to Year 6, PSHCE is taught through the half-termly SCARF units: Me and My Relationships, Valuing Difference, Keeping Safe, Rights and Respect, Being my Best, and Growing and Changing.
Relationships and Health Education
Relationships and Health Education is taught as part of our PSHCE curriculum. Pupils learn about families, friendships, respectful relationships, online relationships, being safe, mental wellbeing, physical health, healthy choices, puberty and growing up.
Learning is carefully sequenced and age-appropriate. Pupils are taught the correct vocabulary they need to understand their bodies, keep themselves safe and speak to a trusted adult if they are worried or unsure.
Vocabulary and subject talk
Vocabulary is taught explicitly in every unit. Pupils learn and revisit important vocabulary such as feelings, friendship, respect, difference, bullying, responsibility, rights, safety, risk, privacy, consent, wellbeing, healthy, puberty, trusted adult and community.
This helps pupils explain their thinking clearly, talk about emotions and relationships, understand how to stay safe and ask for help when needed. Teachers model respectful discussion and provide sentence stems where needed so that all pupils can take part with confidence.
Inclusion and Removing Barriers
Pupils may have different levels of confidence, vocabulary, emotional understanding, life experience or readiness to talk about personal and social issues. Some pupils may find discussion, self-reflection, change, relationships or managing feelings more challenging.
We use clear explanations, stories, visual support, repeated vocabulary, structured discussion, social stories, trusted adults and carefully chosen scenarios to make PSHCE meaningful and accessible. Teachers create a safe and respectful environment so that all pupils, including pupils with SEND, can access the same ambitious PSHCE curriculum.
Progression in PSHCE
Our PSHCE progression map shows how pupils build knowledge, vocabulary, confidence, relationship skills and understanding of health, wellbeing and safety from Nursery to Year 6. This will be added to the page once finalised.

Religious Education
At Thames View, Religious Education helps pupils understand beliefs, values, traditions and worldviews. Pupils learn about Christianity and other major world religions, as well as exploring important questions about identity, belonging, community, respect, responsibility and how people choose to live.
Our RE curriculum follows the locally agreed syllabus and is shaped around the needs, context and experiences of pupils at Thames View.
Our Learning
Religious Education
How RE develops Global Citizens
RE helps pupils develop respect, curiosity and understanding of people with different beliefs, cultures and worldviews. Through learning about faith, worship, celebrations, commitment and moral questions, pupils are encouraged to think deeply about what matters to people and how beliefs can shape the way people live.
This supports our aim of developing thoughtful Global Citizens who listen carefully, ask respectful questions, value difference and understand their place within a diverse community and wider world.
Our RE Narrative Threads
Our RE curriculum is organised around three narrative threads. These help pupils revisit important ideas over time, moving from their own experiences of belonging, celebration and community to a wider understanding of religious and non-religious worldviews.
Pupils learn how beliefs can shape identity and give people a sense of belonging. They begin by exploring who is important to them, where they belong and the beliefs represented within their own community. As they move through the school, pupils learn how Christians, Jews, Muslims, Hindus and Sikhs understand belonging, faith, commitment and identity.
Pupils learn how people live out their faith through worship, prayer, celebrations, festivals, stories, places of worship and acts of commitment. They explore how religious practices can bring people together and help communities show love, thanks, respect and care.
Pupils learn that religions and worldviews often explore some of life’s biggest questions. They reflect on ideas such as kindness, forgiveness, responsibility, truth, eternity, commitment, belonging and what it means to live well. This helps pupils think carefully, listen to others and express their own ideas respectfully.
In RE, pupils revisit prior learning before being introduced to new knowledge, vocabulary and ideas. They learn through stories, discussion, artefacts, images, visits, visitors, celebrations, sacred texts and examples of how people practise their faith.
Pupils are taught to think carefully and respectfully by asking questions, making connections, comparing beliefs and practices, reflecting on different viewpoints and explaining their own thinking. Teachers create safe opportunities for pupils to discuss important ideas while showing respect for others.
Vocabulary is taught explicitly in every unit. Pupils learn and revisit important vocabulary such as belief, faith, religion, worldview, worship, prayer, festival, celebration, community, commitment, respect, forgiveness, belonging and responsibility. This helps pupils explain their thinking clearly, talk respectfully about different beliefs and make links to prior learning.
Teachers model high-quality discussion and provide sentence stems where needed so that all pupils can take part in thoughtful and respectful conversations.
Pupils may have different levels of background knowledge, vocabulary or first-hand experience of different religions, beliefs and places of worship. We use stories, artefacts, photographs, videos, visits, visitors, discussion and carefully chosen resources to make learning meaningful and accessible.
Teachers also use clear explanations, explicit vocabulary teaching, visual support, retrieval, sentence stems and opportunities for reflection so that all pupils, including pupils with SEND, can access the same ambitious RE curriculum.
Religious Education is part of the curriculum for all pupils and supports children’s understanding of beliefs, values, communities and worldviews. Parents and carers have the legal right to withdraw their child from all or part of RE. If you are considering this, please contact the school so that we can discuss your request, share what is being taught and make appropriate arrangements.
Our RE progression map shows how pupils build knowledge, vocabulary, understanding of worldviews and respectful discussion skills from Nursery to Year 6. This will be added to the page once finalised.

Trips & Visitors
Our Learning
Personal Development
Trips & Visitors
Trips & Visitors at Thames View Primary
At Thames View Primary, learning extends beyond the classroom. Each year, pupils take part in a planned programme of educational trips and visiting experts, giving them meaningful experiences that deepen understanding, build cultural capital and create lasting memories. These opportunities strengthen teamwork, curiosity and a sense of community.
Our Annual Offer: 2 Trips & 1 Visitor
Every year group benefits from:
Two curriculum-linked trips
One visiting workshop, speaker or specialist experience
Where possible, our main curriculum trips are scheduled on Hook Day, usually the first Monday of each term. This helps launch new learning with excitement and purpose, giving pupils an immediate, immersive start to their topic.
Curriculum Trips
Curriculum trips are carefully planned to support the learning taking place that term. They may be used to:
Launch a new topic on Hook Day
Support learning mid-unit, providing real-world context
Celebrate the end of a unit, consolidating knowledge through memorable experiences
Each trip is chosen to strengthen the knowledge, skills and vocabulary pupils are developing in class.
Local Learning-Area Visits
In addition to the two main trips, pupils may also take part in short local visits when they naturally support everyday learning. These might include:
A visit to a place of worship
A walk to a local landmark or community space
Fieldwork or observation activities within the local area
These visits are usually shorter, low-cost and closely tied to the curriculum, helping pupils connect their learning to the community around them.
Visitors to School
Every year group also enjoys one high-quality visitor experience, such as:
Workshops led by artists, authors or STEM specialists
Talks from community figures or subject experts
Hands-on sessions that bring a topic to life
Visitors provide expert knowledge, fresh perspectives and engaging activities without leaving the school site.

pageCache.pageTitle: Thames View Primary School - Wellbeing Hub
pageCache.text:
Wellbeing Hub
At Thames View Primary School, we recognise that children need to feel safe, secure and ready to learn before they can achieve their best. Our Wellbeing Hub provides targeted support for pupils who may need additional help with their emotional wellbeing, relationships, behaviour, communication, regulation or confidence.
The Hub is an important part of our wider approach to inclusion. Its purpose is not simply to respond when things go wrong, but to identify barriers early, provide the right support and help children develop the skills they need to become increasingly confident and independent.
Our Learning
Personal Development
Wellbeing Hub
What does the Wellbeing Hub do?
The support provided by the Hub is carefully matched to individual needs. This can include:
Trusted adult check-ins – regular opportunities for children to talk, reflect, seek reassurance and develop a positive relationship with a trusted adult.
Nurture support – structured support to develop confidence, emotional understanding, relationships and readiness to learn.
Emotional regulation support – helping children recognise their emotions, understand what happens when they become overwhelmed and develop strategies to regulate themselves.
Sensory circuits – movement-based activities designed to help some children regulate and prepare for learning.
Social skills groups – opportunities to practise communication, cooperation, friendship and positive interaction with others.
Transition support – additional preparation and reassurance for children experiencing anxiety or difficulty with changes in class, year group, adults or routines.
Lunchtime support – targeted support to help children manage less structured parts of the school day and develop positive relationships and routines.
Individualised support – where appropriate, the Hub works alongside class staff, the SENCO, senior leaders and families to put specific strategies in place for individual children.
The provision changes according to the needs of our pupils. Support may be delivered individually, in small groups or through planned strategies within the classroom and wider school environment.
Why do we have a Wellbeing Hub?
We believe that behaviour, attendance, relationships and emotional wellbeing are closely connected to children's ability to learn.
When a child is finding something difficult, we want to understand what is getting in the way rather than simply focusing on the behaviour we can see. Our approach is based on identifying needs early, putting appropriate support in place and checking whether that support is making a difference.
This is reflected in our Thames View Inclusion Framework, which provides a consistent approach to identifying need, providing support and reviewing impact. It encourages staff to start with strong universal provision, identify emerging concerns early and increase support when this is necessary.
The Hub therefore works closely with classroom staff. Support is most effective when the strategies used by the Hub are understood and reinforced throughout the school day. Our aim is always to help children transfer the skills they develop through intervention into their classroom, playground and wider school life.
What difference can the Hub make?
The impact of the Hub is not measured simply by whether a child attends a session. We look for changes in the things that matter to the child.
This might include a child becoming more confident, managing a transition more successfully, developing friendships, recognising their emotions, using regulation strategies, responding more positively to adults or becoming increasingly independent.
Provision is reviewed regularly. Where a child has made sustained progress, support can be reduced or brought to an end. Where a child's needs become more complex, support can be increased or adapted.
This means that children are not given a fixed label or simply placed on a programme. The level of support reflects what they need at that point in time.
Working together
The Wellbeing Hub does not work in isolation. Effective support depends on strong communication between children, families, class staff and the wider inclusion team.
We work together to understand each child's strengths and needs, agree appropriate strategies and review their impact. Where school-based support is not enough, we can also work with families and relevant external professionals to seek further advice or support.
Our ultimate aim is simple: to help every child feel safe, included, valued and able to succeed.

Clubs & Activities
Our Learning
Clubs & Activities
Clubs
At Thames View Primary, we are proud to offer a wide range of exciting clubs and activities for our pupils. These take place before school, during lunchtime, and after school, giving children plenty of opportunities to explore new interests, make friends, have fun and stay active.
Each term, parents receive an invitation outlining the clubs available for the following term. You can also view our planned offer for the year below. Please note that, on occasion, circumstances may require us to adjust the club programme.
Fair Access for All Pupils
We want every child to have the chance to take part in our clubs. In some cases, we may invite pupils directly to ensure that as many children as possible across the school can participate.
If a club becomes oversubscribed, children who were not successful will be given priority in the next term’s allocation.
Club Times
To help families plan, all school‑run clubs follow standardised timings:
All clubs dismiss from the KS2 playground, making it easier for parents to collect siblings at the same time.
Before School: 08:00 – 08:35

Termly Club Enrolment
With the exception of Young Voices and LAMDA, all clubs reset each term and open to new children. This ensures that as many pupils as possible have the opportunity to join throughout the year. LAMDA will reset after February half term. Clubs are bookable via Arbor.

Personal Development
Belonging, Ambition, Care
At Thames View Primary, we believe that education is about more than academic achievement. We want every child to develop as a confident, curious and responsible Global Citizen who understands themselves, values others and feels a strong sense of belonging.
Our Personal Development curriculum supports pupils to develop the knowledge, skills, attitudes and character they need to thrive. Through our curriculum and wider school life, children learn how to look after themselves, build positive relationships, make responsible choices and contribute positively to their school, community and the wider world.
Our approach is rooted in our ethos of belonging, ambition and care and shaped by our three core values:
Respect: We teach pupils to value themselves, others and the world around them. Children learn to appreciate difference, celebrate the achievements of others, build positive relationships and treat people with kindness and dignity.
Responsibility: We help pupils understand that their choices and actions matter. Children develop increasing independence in managing themselves, their behaviour and their responsibilities. They learn how they can make a positive contribution to their school, their community and the wider world.
Resilience: We encourage pupils to approach challenges with confidence and determination. Children learn that mistakes and setbacks are a natural part of learning. They develop perseverance, self-belief and the resilience to overcome difficulties and keep moving forward.
Through Personal Development, we aim to ensure that every child leaves Thames View with strong character, a sense of belonging, confidence in who they are and an understanding of their place in the world. We want our pupils to be ambitious for themselves and others, curious about the world around them and ready to make positive choices and meaningful contributions as responsible Global Citizens.
Our Learning
Personal Development
PSHE
Our Personal Development (PD) curriculum, is delivered through a number of complimentary and supporting means. In the first instance, each class has a PSHE (Personal, Social and Health Education) lesson each week, either in a single lesson or spread over the week in short sessions. These lessons follow the SCARF syllabus and include the following units:
PSHE lessons feature discussion opportunities and are intended to be supporting, affirming and empowering sessions for the children. Often, these lessons occur at times opportune to helping the children reflect on their learning and relationships as experienced that very day. Our PSHE curriculum includes lessons on E-Safety and Relationships and Health Education (RHE).
Me and My Relationships
Valuing Difference
Keeping Myself Safe
Rights and Respect
Being My Best
Growing and Changing
RE
The children learn about and explore different beliefs and traditions through our well established RE Discovery curriculum. This syllabus enables the children to learn about religions such as Christianity, Judaism, Islam, Hinduism and Buddhism. In RE, we aim to inform children about different religions and then encourage them to share their own opinions and experiences.
Trips & Visitors
Personal Development at Thames View Primary is further enriched through an extensive programme of trips and visitors, designed to give pupils a wide and varied range of experiences beyond the classroom. These experiences help children to develop their understanding of themselves, their community and the wider world, while building their confidence, curiosity and sense of belonging.
Teachers carefully contextualise trips and visits so that pupils understand their purpose and can make meaningful connections between what they experience and what they learn in school. Children are encouraged to ask questions, explore new ideas and appreciate people, places, cultures and experiences that may be different from their own.
Our trips and visitors also provide opportunities for pupils to develop Respect, Responsibility and Resilience. They learn to represent their school positively, show consideration for others, take responsibility for themselves and respond confidently to new and unfamiliar experiences. Shared experiences also strengthen relationships between pupils and help to build a strong sense of community.
Importantly, our trips and visitors programme is closely aligned with our academic curriculum. Experiences are carefully selected to enrich and bring learning to life, giving pupils opportunities to apply their knowledge, deepen their understanding and develop a genuine curiosity about the world around them.
Through these experiences, we aim to broaden pupils' horizons and help them become confident, curious and responsible Global Citizens who value their community and understand their place within the wider world.
Assemblies
Pupils participate in weekly Celebration assemblies where they are rewarded for showing the school values and achieving in their learning over the week. Additionally, other assemblies take place for such events as: Harvest, Christmas, Easter, Mental Health Awareness Week, World Book Day, Number Day and more.
Wellbeing
Our Personal Development curriculum is further supported by our Wellbeing Team, who provide targeted support to help pupils develop the skills, confidence and emotional understanding they need to thrive. The team works closely with pupils to support their wellbeing, behaviour and readiness to learn, helping them to develop positive relationships, manage challenges and become increasingly independent.
Our Home School Support Worker works closely with families, helping to strengthen the partnership between home and school and providing support where families may need additional guidance or assistance. The school also works with external services, including counselling and other specialist support, to ensure that pupils and families can access appropriate support when required.
Through targeted interventions and nurture-based activities, pupils are supported to develop their interpersonal skills, emotional awareness, independence and resilience.
Our school dogs, based in the Wellbeing Hub, also play an important role in supporting pupils' wellbeing. They provide a calm and welcoming presence and help children to feel settled, develop confidence and build positive relationships. Caring for and interacting with the dogs also provides valuable opportunities for pupils to develop empathy, compassion and responsibility.
Through this work, we help ensure that pupils feel known, valued and supported, enabling them to develop the confidence and skills they need to thrive as individuals and as responsible Global Citizens.
Thames View Primary School is an inclusive environment. We ensure that there is equal opportunity for all irrespective of age, disability, gender reassignment, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation. Our PD curriculum promotes the understanding that difference is a positive and that individual characteristics make people unique.
Personal Development at Thames View, delivered through curriculum, assemblies, visits, discussion and literature, develops and deepens pupils' understanding of the fundamental British Values of democracy, individual liberty, the rule of law and mutual respect and tolerance. Pupils explore school and class expectations with teachers and each other, take part in voting for House Captains and can become a part of the School Council.

Assemblies
Assemblies at Thames View
Assemblies are an important part of life at Thames View Primary. They provide opportunities for children to come together as a school community, celebrate success and reflect on the values and expectations that help us to be the best we can be.
Each week, our Celebration Assemblies recognise the achievements and efforts of children across the school. KS1 and KS2 have separate assemblies, allowing the content and celebrations to be appropriate for each age group.
Children receive certificates for achievement and progress in Reading, Writing and Maths, as well as our Star of the Week award for children who have demonstrated our school values of Respect, Responsibility and Resilience. We also celebrate participation and achievement in PE, including sporting performance and excellent PE kit, as well as class attendance.
In Years 3 and 4, we recognise children who have achieved excellent results through Times Table Rock Stars, celebrating both achievement and the commitment that children show to developing their mathematical fluency.
Throughout the year, we also hold special assemblies linked to important events and experiences, including Christmas, Remembrance Day, World Book Day and Enterprise Week. These give children opportunities to learn, reflect, perform and celebrate together.
Our assemblies are positive and purposeful occasions. They help children to recognise their own achievements and those of others, develop confidence and pride in their school community and understand that effort, kindness, responsibility and resilience are all worthy of celebration.
Assemblies usually begin and end with music, creating a warm and celebratory atmosphere and marking assemblies as a special part of the school week.

Relationships & Health Education
Relationships Education focusses on teaching the fundamental characteristics of positive relationships, with particular emphasis on friendships, family and relationships with other children and adults, both on and offline. At Thames View we believe it is important to give the children the essential skills for building enjoyable, respectful and non-exploitative relationships. Health Education focusses on good physical and mental health, how to stay safe on and offline, and the importance of healthy relationships. At Thames View we will ensure pupils are taught about the benefits of a healthier lifestyle, what determines their physical health and how to build mental resilience and wellbeing.

Parent Forums
Parent Forums at Thames View Primary School
At Thames View Primary School, we believe that strong partnerships between home and school are key to every child’s success. Our Parent Forums provide a welcoming space for parents and carers to come together, share ideas, and discuss important topics that impact our children and community.
These sessions are designed to:
Support families with practical tips and strategies for everyday challenges.
Strengthen communication between parents and the school.
Build a community where everyone feels heard, valued, and involved.
Each forum focusses on a specific theme – from supporting children’s wellbeing and learning at home to preparing for key transitions.
Whether you want to listen, learn, or contribute your own experiences, our Parent Forums are a fantastic opportunity to work together to give our children the best possible start.
✨ Your voice matters. Join us and be part of the conversation!

Remote Learning
In line with government expectations, at Thames View Primary School we aim for our Remote Curriculum to:
EYFS: Learning activities will be varied and appropriate to the age and stage of the children. KS1: At least 3 hours of remote provision. KS2: At least 4 hours of remote provision.
In KS1 and KS2, this does not mean this will be 3 or 4 hours or teacher contact. The time is made up of some instructional time, independent learning time for research, practice or consolidation, feedback or direct work with teachers. At Thames View, we recognise that not all pupils will be able to access remote education without adult support and that not all children will have the same access to online learning. We will work with families to support their children in achieving all that they can.

Curriculum
Our Learning
Belonging Here. Shaping the World.
At Thames View Primary School, our curriculum is designed to help every child belong, achieve and thrive. We want pupils to develop strong academic foundations, a love of learning and the confidence to understand themselves, their community and the wider world.
Our vision is to develop pupils as confident, curious and responsible Global Citizens. Children begin by learning about their own lives, families, school and local community, before broadening their understanding of Kent, the wider UK and the world beyond.
Through our values of Respect, Responsibility and Resilience, pupils learn to value themselves and others, take responsibility for their choices and develop the confidence to face challenges. We want every child to leave Thames View with the knowledge, character and ambition to help shape a fairer, healthier and more sustainable future.
We offer a broad, ambitious and carefully sequenced curriculum that helps pupils build knowledge, vocabulary and skills over time. Reading, discussion and high-quality texts are central to this, giving pupils the language and confidence they need to think deeply, explain their ideas and make meaningful links across subjects.
Our curriculum is organised around a clear journey. Pupils begin with what is familiar — themselves, their families, school and local community — before learning about Kent, the wider UK, different societies, cultures, environments and global issues. As they move through school, they revisit important themes such as identity, diversity, belonging, sustainability, interconnection, responsibility and social action with increasing depth.
Subjects are carefully planned so that pupils develop both subject-specific knowledge and wider understanding. Geography helps pupils understand place, environment and interconnection. History helps pupils understand everyday life, society and legacy. RE, PSHE, Computing, Science, the Arts, DT, PE and Forest School all contribute to pupils’ understanding of themselves, others and the world around them.
Me, my family and my world
Who am I and who is important to me?
My school, my community, my place
What makes a community and how can we help it?
Development Matters & Early Years Framework
Our local area: Kent
What makes our local area special?
How is it connected to other places?
How are places across the UK similar and different?
An interconnected world
How are people, places and environments connected?
Our shared responsibility
How do our choices affect people, places and the planet?
Societies in contact
How do societies interact, influence and change one another?
The world we want to create
How can we help shape a fairer, healthier and more sustainable world?
Learning at Thames View is brought to life through carefully chosen texts, practical experiences, fieldwork, outdoor learning, educational visits, visitors, pupil leadership and community links. These opportunities are not add-ons; they are planned to deepen pupils’ understanding and help them connect learning to real people, places and issues.
Our curriculum supports all pupils, including those with SEND and those who may face barriers to learning. Teachers use clear explanations, explicit vocabulary teaching, retrieval, modelling, visual support, discussion and carefully planned adaptations so that every child can access ambitious learning.
Through subjects, enrichment and wider school life, pupils learn that they have a voice and a role to play. They are encouraged to ask questions, think critically, show respect for different perspectives and take responsibility for their school, community and wider world.
Across the curriculum, pupils revisit four key Global Citizen threads:
Belief, Identity and Belonging
Understanding who we are and the communities we belong to.
Societies and Interconnection
Understanding how local, national and global communities are connected.
Understanding how human choices affect the planet
Voice, Action and Responsibility
Understanding how we can make a positive difference
